story: “Pitfall” for the Atari describes its whole world in a single byte
text: I think much of this is explained at a high level in this talk from the original game designer: Pitfall Classic Postmortem With David Crane Panel at GDC 2011 (Atari 2600). [VIDEO] I haven't seen it in a while (will rewatch now), but I remember him going over how he was able to create so many levels in such a tiny space. I love these sorts of examples of breakthrough tech products that were the result of a developer figuring out how to do something that seemed impossible. Much of Apple's early success, for example, could be attributed to this.

story: Atari 2600 Hardware Design: Making Something Out of (Almost) Nothing
text: Can't remember if I read it here recently, or on reddit, but this conference session with David Crane on Pitfall/Atari is pretty good. He doesn't as technical as some folks may want, but there's some coolness in just hearing him explain this in person. Couple of interesting Q&A bits towards the end too. [VIDEO]
And in Pitfall, David Crane basically used a random number generator with a predefined seed to generate the world ( [VIDEO] starting at the 22:12 mark).
